title: Paths Where Both Ends Are the Highest

concept.title: Add the nodes from the lowest value up; at a value, nodes that sit in the same group are connected through lower or equal nodes
body: Every node of a tree has a value. A path is *good* if its two end nodes have the **same value** and **no node on the path has a larger value** than that. A path of a single node is good. Count the good paths (a path is the same as its reverse; count it once).

Process the nodes in **increasing order of value**, group by group (all nodes with the same value together). Maintain a union-find of the nodes processed so far that are connected by edges whose both ends have been processed. For a value `x`: first **connect** every node of value `x` with each neighbour whose value is at most `x`. Now two nodes of value `x` are in the same union-find group exactly when the path between them uses only nodes of value at most `x` (no higher node): that path is good. So if `c` nodes of value `x` fall into one group, they make `c * (c - 1) / 2` good paths between them. Add the `n` single-node paths separately.
The answer can be large (if all values are equal on a path of 20000 nodes, about 2 * 10^8 pairs), so use 64-bit integers. The time is O(n log n).

statement: A tree with `n` nodes has a value at every node. A path in the tree is good if its two ends have the same value and no node on the path has a larger value than that. A path of a single node is good. Count the good paths; a path and its reverse are the same path.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes and the number of edges (`m = n - 1`).
The second line has `n` numbers: the value of every node.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge of the tree.
outputFormat: Print the number of good paths.
constraints: m = n - 1, and the edges form a tree

examples.note: There are 5 paths of one node, and the path 2-1-3-5 joins the two nodes with the value 3 through nodes of lower value: 6.

hints: Process the nodes in increasing order of value, handling all nodes of the same value together.
First join each node of the current value with the neighbours of lower or equal value, using union-find.
Count the nodes of the current value in every group: c nodes make c * (c - 1) / 2 good paths. Add n for the single nodes.

solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

parent = []
size = []

def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

def union(a, b):
    a, b = find(a), find(b)
    if a == b:
        return False
    if size[a] < size[b]:
        a, b = b, a
    parent[b] = a
    size[a] += size[b]
    return True

n, m = map(int, input().split())
value = list(map(int, input().split()))
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
parent.extend(range(n + 1))
size.extend([1] * (n + 1))
order = sorted(range(1, n + 1), key=lambda v: value[v - 1])
total = n
i = 0
while i < n:
    j = i
    x = value[order[i] - 1]
    while j < n and value[order[j] - 1] == x:
        j += 1
    group = order[i:j]
    for v in group:
        for w in adj[v]:
            if value[w - 1] <= x:
                union(v, w)
    count = {}
    for v in group:
        root = find(v)
        count[root] = count.get(root, 0) + 1
    total += sum(c * (c - 1) // 2 for c in count.values())
    i = j
print(total)
